UNIT 1 · WEEK 1
Your Starting Line 🦉

An honest snapshot of where you're starting — no right answers. Just a sentence or two for each prompt below.

1.Introduce yourself. Who are you, and what do you like to do? (Also post this part to the class discussion.)
2.How active are you right now? Be honest — there's no wrong answer.
3.One healthy habit you already have, and one you want to build.
4.Who's in your corner to help you get healthier this year?
📤 Submit below: type it in the box, upload a file, or record a short video/audio — your choice.
🦉 Optima Academy Online — HOPE · Unit 1

UNIT 1 · WEEK 2
Wellness Self-Portrait 🦉

Your honest baseline for the year. Three quick parts — be real, not impressive.

1. Rate each dimension 1–5 (1 = low, 5 = thriving):
💪 Physical — __
🧠 Emotional — __
🤝 Social — __
📚 Intellectual — __
🧭 Spiritual — __
🌳 Environmental — __
2.Pick 2 dimensions to grow this year — one sentence on why each matters to you.
3.Name one internet-safety habit you'll keep, and one small goal for the next two weeks.
📤 Submit below: type it, upload a file, or record a short video/audio.
✅ 20 pts: all 6 rated (8) · 2 growth areas with reasons (6) · safety habit (3) · goal (3). Honest beats impressive.
🦉 Optima Academy Online — HOPE · Unit 1

assignments.html:

🏃 UNIT 1 LOG
Activity Log — Weeks 1–2 🦉

This is the PE part of HOPE — real activity you actually do. Log your movement across this unit's two weeks. Aim for moderate-to-vigorous activity on 5+ days a week.

1.Log each session. For every active day, record: date · activity · minutes · intensity (light / moderate / vigorous).
2.Total it up. Add your total active minutes and how many days you moved each week.
3.One-line reflection. How did you feel, and what's one thing you'll adjust next unit?
Log row format:  Date · Activity · Minutes · Intensity  —  e.g., Mon · brisk walk · 25 min · moderate.  Anything that gets you moving counts.
📤 Submit below: type your log in the box, upload a doc/photo/spreadsheet, or export from a fitness app/watch and attach it.
✅ 10 pts: both weeks logged with all fields (6) · 5+ active days/week target (worked toward) (2) · reflection (2). Effort and honesty matter more than the numbers.
🦉 Optima Academy Online — HOPE · Unit 1 · Activity Log

assignments.title: Unit 1 · VR — Build Your Wellness Wheel
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
HOPE
High School · HOPE
🥽 UNIT 1 · VR
Build Your Wellness Wheel 🥽

Make a 3D version of the six dimensions of wellness — and place yourself in it. You'll build this yourself in VR — there's no room to join, just your own space and your creativity. Plan on about 20–30 minutes.

🛠️Build it (in Arthur VR)

Open a blank/personal space and create everything from scratch:

1.Create 6 zones or objects in your space, one for each dimension: physical, emotional, social, intellectual, spiritual, environmental.
2.Label each one (use text panels, signs, or pinned notes).
3.In each zone, place an object that represents a personal strength or a goal for that dimension.
4.Stand in the middle so all six are around you.
📸 Capture & submit: take a screenshot or short screen-recording inside your headset showing what you built, then add a 2–3 sentence reflection: Which dimension's zone was easiest to fill, and which was hardest? What does that tell you about your wellness right now?
💻 No headset? You can build the same thing with a free 3D/whiteboard tool (or even sketch it on paper) and submit a photo with the same reflection. You won't be penalized for not having VR.
✅ 10 pts: built the required pieces (5) · labeled/organized correctly (2) · reflection answered (3).
🦉 Optima Academy Online — HOPE · Unit 1 · VR / Immersive

FITT Plan Draft 🦉

I — light/mod/vigorous
T — __ min/session
T — activity type

Baseline Report + SMART Goals 🦉

Your first major submission. Report your baseline, then set the goals you'll chase this year. Three quick parts.

1.Report your baseline. List your result for each test: cardio (mile/step), push-ups, core (curl-ups/plank), flexibility (sit-and-reach).
2.Name your strength and your priority. Which component is strongest now, and which one will you focus on?
3.Write 2 SMART goals for your priority area(s) — each Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound — and say how you'll track them.
❤️ Cardio — ____
💪 Push-ups — ____
🔁 Core — ____
🤸 Flexibility — ____
💡 SMART goal example: "Reach past my toes on the sit-and-reach within 8 weeks by stretching 10 minutes, 4 days a week."
📤 Submit below: type it (a table works great), upload a file, or record a short video/audio.
✅ 20 pts: all 4 baseline results reported (6) · strength + priority named (4) · 2 complete SMART goals (8) · tracking plan (2).

2-Week Cardio Log 🦉

Your major submission for this unit — and it's mostly doing. Train your heart over two weeks, log each session, then reflect. Three parts.

1.Log your sessions for 2 weeks. For each: date, activity, minutes, and your zone/effort (heart rate, talk test, or RPE). Aim for MVPA on 5+ days a week.
2.Use at least two methods (continuous, interval, fartlek, or cross-training) and note one rest day.
3.Progress note (3–5 sentences): Did it get easier? Did you stay in your zone? What will you adjust next?
Log row format:  Date · Activity · Minutes · Zone/RPE · Note  —  e.g., Mar 3 · jog · 25 min · moderate (talk test) · felt good, less winded than last week.
📤 Submit below: type your log + note in the box, upload a doc/photo/spreadsheet, or export from a fitness app and attach it.
✅ 20 pts: 2 weeks logged with all fields (8) · 5+ active days/week (5) · 2+ methods + a rest day (3) · progress note (4).

assignments.title: Unit 5 · Week 10 — Form Video Submission
assignments.html:
Optima
Academy Online
HOPE

UNIT 5 · WEEK 10
Form Video Submission 🦉

Your major submission: record 3 movements with good form, then coach yourself. It's about control and noticing — not lifting heavy. Two parts.

1.Record 3 movements (a few reps each), one from each: a push, a pull or core, and a legs move. Film from the side. A photo set at key positions works if you can't do video.
2.Self-analyze (3–5 sentences): for each move, which form cues did you nail, and what's one thing to improve next time?
The 5 cues to check yourself against: brace your core · neutral spine · full range of motion · controlled tempo · breathe.
🛡️ Safety: warm up first, use resistance you can control with good form, and clear your space. Good form > heavy load, always.
📤 Submit below: record/upload your video with Media, attach a photo set as a file, and/or type your self-analysis in the text box.
✅ 20 pts: 3 movements across push/pull-or-core/legs (9) · visible control & full range (5) · self-analysis using the cues (6).
🦉 Optima Academy Online — HOPE · Unit 5

Reframe: Health Over Looks 🦉

Body composition is about health, not appearance. Let's make that shift personal. A couple sentences per prompt — be honest and kind to yourself.

1.In your own words, what does "healthy body composition" mean — and how is that different from how a body looks?
2.Name two health behaviors (move, fuel, sleep, stress, hydrate) you can focus on instead of a number on a scale.
3.How does good flexibility/mobility help your everyday life — name one real example?
📤 Submit below: type it, upload a file, or record a short video/audio. No judgment here — this one's just for your own thinking.
🦉 Optima Academy Online — HOPE · Unit 6

assignments.title: Unit 6 · Week 12 — Mobility Routine + Injury-Risk Audit
assignments.html:

UNIT 6 · WEEK 12
Mobility Routine + Injury-Risk Audit 🦉

Your major submission: build a routine you'll use, then coach your own safety. Three parts.

1.Mobility routine. List 3 dynamic warm-up moves and 3 static cool-down holds you'll actually use (note seconds/reps for each).
2.Injury-risk audit. Look at how you train. Name 2 injury risks in your current habits (e.g., skipping warm-ups, ramping too fast, bad surface) and one fix for each.
3.Connect it. Name one health problem that low fitness can cause, and one thing you're doing to lower that risk.
🛡️ Reminder: stretch to mild tension (never pain), warm up before / cool down after, and use RICE for minor strains. Get help for severe or lasting pain.
📤 Submit below: type it in the box, upload a doc/photo, or record a short video walking through your routine.
✅ 20 pts: mobility routine, 3 dynamic + 3 static (8) · 2 risks + fixes (8) · low-fitness/health connection (4).

quizzes.title: Unit 1 Quiz — Orientation & Dimensions of Wellness

questions.text: What does HOPE stand for?

answers.feedback: ❌ Close, but not the official name.
✅ Correct! That's it — Health Opportunities through Physical Education.
❌ Not quite — HOPE is about your own health and PE.
❌ Not quite — the 'PE' stands for Physical Education.

questions.text: The HELP philosophy that the course is built on means:

answers.feedback: ❌ That's not it — HELP isn't about intensity.
❌ No — the course is built around YOU, not experts.

answers.text: Health is for Everyone, for a Lifetime, and it's Personal

answers.feedback: ❌ No — HELP is the course's whole-person philosophy.

questions.text: What is the single best predictor of success in a self-paced course?

answers.feedback: ❌ Nope — talent isn't what carries you in a self-paced course.
❌ Cramming isn't the goal — steady work is.

answers.text: Building a weekly routine you stick to
answers.feedback: ✅ Correct! Exactly — routine beats motivation and talent.
❌ Equipment isn't required, and it's not the predictor.

questions.text: Your activity log records four things about each session. Which is NOT one of them?

answers.feedback: ❌ That IS one of the four — the type of activity.
❌ That IS one of the four — minutes of activity.

answers.text: Exactly how many calories you burned
answers.feedback: ✅ Correct! You don't need exact calories. You log what, how long, how hard, and how it felt.
❌ That IS one of the four — your quick note.

questions.text: What is the course's weekly physical activity target?

answers.text: Moderate-to-vigorous activity on 5 or more days a week
One long workout on the weekend
answers.feedback: ❌ Spreading activity across the week works better.

answers.text: Two hours of exercise every single day
answers.feedback: ❌ That's not the target — and it's not realistic for most.

answers.text: Only on days you have PE class
answers.feedback: ❌ HOPE is about activity BEYOND class time.

questions.text: You don't have a gym or any equipment. What does that mean for this course?

answers.text: You can't complete the activity parts
answers.feedback: ❌ Not true — every activity has another option.

answers.text: Nothing — every activity has no-equipment, small-space options
answers.feedback: ✅ Correct! Right — you build from wherever you are.

answers.text: You must buy equipment before starting

answers.feedback: ❌ Equipment is never required for credit.

answers.feedback: ✅ Correct! Physical, emotional, social, intellectual, spiritual, environmental.
❌ Not quite — the course uses six.

questions.text: Which of these is the best example of emotional wellness?

answers.text: Going for a run to build endurance
Reading about a topic out of curiosity
Using a coping strategy to handle stress
answers.feedback: ✅ Correct! Managing feelings and stress is emotional wellness.

answers.text: Setting your social accounts to private

questions.text: You join a club where you finally click with people who get you. Which dimension does this build most?

answers.feedback: ❌ Spiritual is about meaning and values.
✅ Correct! Relationships and a support network are social wellness.

questions.text: You clean up your room and turn on location privacy on your phone. Which dimension does this support?

answers.feedback: ✅ Correct! Your physical AND digital surroundings are environmental wellness.
❌ Not the best fit — this is about your spaces.
❌ It's about your environment, not relationships.

questions.text: Why do we say the dimensions of wellness are connected?

answers.text: Because you must score high in all six to be healthy
answers.feedback: ❌ Nobody maxes all six — that's not the point.

answers.text: Because a change in one (like poor sleep) can affect the others (like mood and focus)
answers.feedback: ✅ Correct! Pull one lever and the others move.

answers.text: Because they all cost money to improve
Because only physical wellness actually matters
answers.feedback: ❌ All six matter — and they interact.

answers.text: The size of files stored on your phone
The lasting trail of everything you post and do online
answers.feedback: ✅ Correct! And it can stick around for years.

answers.text: A password that protects your accounts
answers.feedback: ❌ That's account security, not your footprint.

answers.text: The number of apps you have installed
answers.feedback: ❌ Not quite — it's about what you leave behind online.

answers.feedback: ✅ Correct! Your address is personally identifiable information.

answers.text: Phishing — a scam designed to trick you

answers.text: A normal message you can ignore safely either way
answers.feedback: ❌ Ignore the link, yes — but recognize it as a scam.

answers.text: Proof the message is from your school
answers.feedback: ❌ Schools don't pressure you with urgent delete threats.

answers.feedback: ❌ Never agree to meet someone you only know online.

answers.text: Share more info to prove you're not scared
answers.feedback: ❌ Never share private info with someone online.
